about: Tuned llama-server settings per model and route, applied by `1bit serve` (docs/recipes.md). A recipe never overrides a flag already on the backend's command line or a variable already set. Every recipe carries the measurement behind it; re-measure with tools/bench.py before changing one.

recipes.why: DFlash2 proposes and verifies whole 8-token blocks, so a non-zero draft p-min discards blocks whose first tokens look unlikely and the loss lands on prose; 0 keeps every block whole. The flag is pinned here rather than left to llama-server's default, because the measurement below is what the recipe is for.
recipes.measured: Qwen3.8-27B UD-Q4_K_XL, 1bit serve --dflash with the Q8_0 drafter, greedy 256-token chats, medians of 3, performance mode, 2026-10-24: p-min 0 gives 56.6 / 30.8 / 20.6 tok/s on code / prose / short (acceptance 0.88 / 0.42 / 0.23); p-min 0.2, 0.4 and 0.6 cut prose to 22.5-23.3. The Q4_K drafter reaches 58.8 on code at p-min 0. Strict placement on: the drafter's graphs run on HRX in one graph split.

recipes.why: The model's own MTP head accepts about two thirds of its three drafts, and acceptance collapses past seven, so a longer verify batch costs more than the extra drafts return. Capping at 3 is what the measurement below is for; do not raise it past 7.
recipes.measured: Qwen3.8-27B UD-Q4_K_XL with its in-file MTP head, greedy 256-token chats, medians of 3, performance mode, 2026-10-24: --mtp-max 3 gives 32.6 / 26.9 / 28.0 tok/s on code / prose / short (12.1 / 12.1 / 12.5 without drafting). --mtp-max 7 --mtp-p-min 0 gives 37.9 / 22.4 / 22.4 and --mtp-max 15 33.6 / 14.9 / 13.5, with 0.17-0.60 acceptance past 8 drafts.
